# SYS003 sys-binding-conflict

Bindings contradict each other or an operand does not resolve.

## What it does

One rule with a kind in each message: directive-directive (two directives give one identity two nodes), directive-selector (a directive's node is not among the most specific Must selectors), ambiguous-singleton (a shape, ref or single runnable clause names several identities; several runnable clauses are fine, each is judged alone), end-owner (a flow end's code is owned by a node other than the flow's endpoint), dangling-operand and ambiguous-operand (a grimble:binds operand names nothing or several things). Unresolved for end-owner when the owner is only May.

## Why it matters

Bindings come from several sources. When they disagree, the model says one thing and the code another, and the check cannot tell which to trust.

## Remedy

Fix the binding the message names: the directive, the selector, or the flow end.

## Examples

### Fires case 1

```grmb expect=fire file=design/m.grmb
grimble = "2";
module m;

node a : trusted {
  owns "a/**";
}
node b : trusted {
  owns "b/**";
}
node d : trusted {
  owns "design/**";
}
flow bad : a -> b {
  producer "a/lib.rs::send";
  consumer "a/lib.rs::send";
}
```

### Clean case 2

```grmb expect=clean file=design/m.grmb
grimble = "2";
module m;

node a : trusted {
  owns "a/**";
}
node b : trusted {
  owns "b/**";
}
node d : trusted {
  owns "design/**";
}
flow ok : a -> b {
  producer "a/lib.rs::send";
  consumer "b/lib.rs::recv";
}
```
